newsitem.title: GERMANY: German 1996 motor vehicle output up four percent.
newsitem.headline: German 1996 motor vehicle output up four percent.

text.p: German motor vehicle production grew by four percent to 4.84 million units in 1996, helped by an eight percent increase in exports to 2.84 million, the VDA Automobile Industry Association said.
Car production also grew four percent, to 4.54 million vehicles, with car exports up seven percent at 2.67 million, the VDA said in a statement.
New motor vehicle registrations -- a measure of domestic demand -- rose five percent to 3.76 million units last year.
In December, motor vehicle output fell one percent from the year-earlier month to 339,000.
Domestic new orders for cars fell 21 percent in December compared with December 1995, while orders from abroad rose by three percent, the VDA said.
The output of trucks weighing up to six tonnes rose by 10 percent in 1996, with exports up 26 percent. Heavier trucks saw production shrink by 15 percent, with exports down 10 percent.
